765: // DoLoopbackAuthorization performs the log in into the identity provider
766: // opening a browser and using a redirect_uri in a loopback IP address
767: // (http://127.0.0.1:port or http://[::1]:port).
768: func (o *oauth) DoLoopbackAuthorization() (*token, error) {
769: 	srv, err := o.NewServer()
770: 	if err != nil {
771: 		return nil, err
772: 	}
773: 	// Update server url if --listen-url is set
774: 	if o.CallbackListenerURL != "" {
775: 		o.redirectURI = o.CallbackListenerURL
776: 	} else {
777: 		o.redirectURI = srv.URL
778: 	}
779: 	defer srv.Close()
780: 
781: 	// Get auth url and open it in a browser
782: 	authURL, err := o.Auth()
783: 	if err != nil {
784: 		return nil, err
785: 	}
786: 
787: 	if skipBrowser := os.Getenv("STEP_OPEN_BROWSER") == "0"; skipBrowser {
788: 		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, authURL)
789: 	} else {
790: 		if err := exec.OpenInBrowser(authURL, o.browser); err != nil {
791: 			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "Cannot open a web browser on your platform.")
792: 			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr)
793: 			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "Open a local web browser and visit:")
794: 			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr)
795: 			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, authURL)
796: 			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr)
797: 		} else {
798: 			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "Your default web browser has been opened to visit:")
799: 			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr)
800: 			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, authURL)
801: 			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr)
802: 		}
803: 	}
804: 
805: 	// Wait for response and return the token
806: 	select {
807: 	case tok := <-o.tokCh:
808: 		return tok, nil
809: 	case err := <-o.errCh:
810: 		return nil, err
811: 	case <-time.After(2 * time.Minute):
812: 		return nil, errors.New("oauth command timed out, please try again")
813: 	}
814: }

861: // DoDeviceAuthorization gets a token from the IDP using the OAuth 2.0
862: // Device Authorization Grant. https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8628
863: func (o *oauth) DoDeviceAuthorization() (*token, error) {
864: 	// Identify the Device
865: 	data := url.Values{}
866: 	data.Set("client_id", o.clientID)
867: 	data.Set("client_secret", o.clientSecret)
868: 	data.Set("scope", o.scope)
869: 
870: 	resp, err := postForm(o.deviceAuthzEndpoint, data)
871: 	if err != nil {
872: 		return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "http failure to identify device")
873: 	}
874: 	defer resp.Body.Close()
875: 	b, err := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
876: 	if err != nil {
877: 		return nil, err
878: 	}
879: 
880: 	if resp.StatusCode >= 400 {
881: 		var e struct {
882: 			Error string
883: 		}
884: 		if err := json.NewDecoder(bytes.NewReader(b)).Decode(&e); err != nil {
885: 			return nil, errors.Wrapf(err, "could not parse http body: %s", string(b))
886: 		}
887: 	}
888: 
889: 	var idr identifyDeviceResponse
890: 	if err := json.NewDecoder(bytes.NewReader(b)).Decode(&idr); err != nil {
891: 		return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failure decoding device authz response to JSON")
892: 	}
893: 
894: 	shouldPrintCode := true
895: 	switch {
896: 	case idr.VerificationURIComplete != "":
897: 		// Prefer VerificationURIComplete if present for user convenience
898: 		idr.VerificationURI = idr.VerificationURIComplete
899: 		shouldPrintCode = false
900: 	case idr.VerificationURI != "":
901: 		// do nothing
902: 	case idr.VerificationURL != "":
903: 		// NOTE this is a hack for Google, because their API returns the attribute
904: 		// 'verification_url` rather than `verification_uri`.
905: 		idr.VerificationURI = idr.VerificationURL
906: 	default:
907: 		return nil, errors.Errorf("device code response from server missing 'verification_uri' parameter. http body response: %s", string(b))
908: 	}
909: 
910: 	if idr.Interval <= 0 {
911: 		idr.Interval = defaultDeviceAuthzInterval
912: 	}
913: 
914: 	if shouldPrintCode {
915: 		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Visit %s and enter the code:\n", idr.VerificationURI)
916: 		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, idr.UserCode)
917: 	} else {
918: 		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Visit %s:\n", idr.VerificationURI)
919: 	}
920: 
921: 	// Poll the Token endpoint until the user completes the flow.
922: 	data = url.Values{}
923: 	data.Set("client_id", o.clientID)
924: 	data.Set("client_secret", o.clientSecret)
925: 	data.Set("grant_type", "urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code")
926: 	data.Set("device_code", idr.DeviceCode)
927: 
928: 	endPollIn := defaultDeviceAuthzExpiresIn
929: 	if idr.ExpiresIn > 0 {
930: 		expiresIn := time.Duration(idr.ExpiresIn) * time.Second
931: 		if expiresIn < endPollIn {
932: 			endPollIn = expiresIn
933: 		}
934: 	}
935: 
936: 	t := time.NewTimer(endPollIn)
937: 	defer t.Stop()
938: 	for {
939: 		select {
940: 		case <-time.After(time.Duration(idr.Interval) * time.Second):
941: 			tok, err := o.deviceAuthzTokenPoll(data)
942: 			if errors.Is(err, errHTTPToken) {
943: 				continue
944: 			} else if err != nil {
945: 				return nil, err
946: 			}
947: 			return tok, nil
948: 		case <-t.C:
949: 			return nil, errors.New("device authorization grant expired")
950: 		}
951: 	}
952: }

956: func (o *oauth) deviceAuthzTokenPoll(data url.Values) (*token, error) {
957: 	resp, err := postForm(o.tokenEndpoint, data)
958: 	if err != nil {
959: 		return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "error doing POST to /token endpoint")
960: 	}
961: 	defer resp.Body.Close()

963: 	if err != nil {
964: 		return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "error reading HTTP response body from /token endpoint")
965: 	}
966: 
967: 	switch {
968: 	case resp.StatusCode == http.StatusOK:
969: 		tok := token{}

971: 			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "error parsing JSON /token response")
972: 		}
973: 		return &tok, nil
974: 	case resp.StatusCode >= http.StatusBadRequest && resp.StatusCode < http.StatusInternalServerError:
975: 		return nil, errHTTPToken

988: 	}
989: 	priv, err := x509.ParsePKCS8PrivateKey(block.Bytes)
990: 	if err != nil {
991: 		return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "error parsing private key")
992: 	}
993: 
994: 	// Add claims
995: 	now := int(time.Now().Unix())
996: 	c := map[string]interface{}{
997: 		"aud":   o.tokenEndpoint,
998: 		"nbf":   now,
999: 		"iat":   now,
1000: 		"exp":   now + 3600,
1001: 		"iss":   issuer,
1002: 		"scope": o.scope,
1003: 	}
1004: 
1005: 	so := new(jose.SignerOptions)
1006: 	so.WithType("JWT")
1007: 	so.WithHeader("kid", o.clientID)
1008: 
1009: 	// Sign JWT
1010: 	signer, err := jose.NewSigner(jose.SigningKey{
1011: 		Algorithm: "RS256",
1012: 		Key:       priv,
1013: 	}, so)
1014: 	if err != nil {
1015: 		return nil, errors.Wrapf(err, "error creating JWT signer")
1016: 	}
1017: 
1018: 	raw, err := jose.Signed(signer).Claims(c).CompactSerialize()
1019: 	if err != nil {
1020: 		return nil, errors.Wrapf(err, "error serializing JWT")
1021: 	}
1022: 
1023: 	// Construct the POST request to fetch the OAuth token.
1024: 	params := url.Values{
1025: 		"assertion":  []string{raw},
1026: 		"grant_type": []string{jwtBearerUrn},

1033: 	}

1036: 	var tok token
1037: 	if err := json.NewDecoder(resp.Body).Decode(&tok); err != nil {
1038: 		return nil, errors.WithStack(err)
1039: 	}

1090: // ServeHTTP is the handler that performs the OAuth 2.0 dance and returns the
1091: // tokens using channels.
1092: func (o *oauth) ServeHTTP(w http.ResponseWriter, req *http.Request) {
1093: 	if req.URL.Path != o.CallbackPath {
1094: 		http.NotFound(w, req)
1095: 		return
1096: 	}
1097: 
1098: 	if req.Method == http.MethodOptions {
1099: 		w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK)
1100: 		w.Write(nil)
1101: 		return
1102: 	}
1103: 
1104: 	q := req.URL.Query()
1105: 	errStr := q.Get("error")
1106: 	if errStr != "" {
1107: 		o.badRequest(w, "Failed to authenticate: "+errStr)
1108: 		return
1109: 	}
1110: 
1111: 	if o.implicit {
1112: 		o.implicitHandler(w, req)
1113: 		return
1114: 	}
1115: 
1116: 	code, state := q.Get("code"), q.Get("state")
1117: 	if code == "" || state == "" {
1118: 		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Invalid request received: http://%s%s\n", req.RemoteAddr, req.URL.String()) // #nosec G705 -- terminal output
1119: 		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "You may have an app or browser plugin that needs to be turned off\n")
1120: 		http.Error(w, "400 bad request", http.StatusBadRequest)
1121: 		return
1122: 	}
1123: 
1124: 	if code == "" {
1125: 		o.badRequest(w, "Failed to authenticate: missing or invalid code")
1126: 		return
1127: 	}
1128: 
1129: 	if state == "" || state != o.state {
1130: 		o.badRequest(w, "Failed to authenticate: missing or invalid state")
1131: 		return
1132: 	}
1133: 
1134: 	tok, err := o.Exchange(o.tokenEndpoint, code)
1135: 	if err != nil {
1136: 		o.badRequest(w, "Failed exchanging authorization code: "+err.Error())
1137: 		return
1138: 	}
1139: 	if tok.Err != "" || tok.ErrDesc != "" {
1140: 		o.badRequest(w, fmt.Sprintf("Failed exchanging authorization code: %s. %s", tok.Err, tok.ErrDesc))
1141: 		return
1142: 	}
1143: 
1144: 	if o.terminalRedirect != "" {
1145: 		http.Redirect(w, req, o.terminalRedirect, http.StatusFound)
1146: 	} else {

1198: func (o *oauth) Auth() (string, error) {
1199: 	u, err := url.Parse(o.authzEndpoint)
1200: 	if err != nil {
1201: 		return "", errors.WithStack(err)
1202: 	}
1203: 
1204: 	q := u.Query()
1205: 	q.Add("client_id", o.clientID)
1206: 	q.Add("redirect_uri", o.redirectURI)
1207: 	if o.implicit {

1213: 		q.Add("code_challenge", base64.RawURLEncoding.EncodeToString(s256[:]))

1215: 	q.Add("scope", o.scope)

1217: 		q.Add("prompt", o.prompt)
1218: 	}
1219: 	q.Add("state", o.state)
1220: 	q.Add("nonce", o.nonce)

1227: 		}
1228: 	}

	"github.com/smallstep/cli/flags"
	"github.com/smallstep/cli/utils/cautils"
)

func bootstrapCommand() cli.Command {
	return cli.Command{
		Name:   "bootstrap",
		Action: command.ActionFunc(bootstrapAction),
		Usage:  "initialize the environment to use the CA commands",
		UsageText: `**step ca bootstrap**
[**--ca-url**=<uri>] [**--fingerprint**=<fingerprint>] [**--install**]
[**--team**=<name>] [**--authority**=<name>] [**--team-url**=<uri>] [**--redirect-url**=<uri>]
[**--context**=<name>] [**--profile**=<name>]
[**--authority**=<name>] [**--team-authority**=<sub-domain>]`,
		Description: `**step ca bootstrap** downloads the root certificate from the certificate
authority and sets up the current environment to use it.

Bootstrap will store the root certificate in <$STEPPATH/certs/root_ca.crt> and
create a configuration file in <$STEPPATH/configs/defaults.json> with the CA
url, the root certificate location and its fingerprint.

After the bootstrap, ca commands do not need to specify the flags
--ca-url, --root or --fingerprint if we want to use the same environment.

## EXAMPLES

Bootstrap using the CA url and a fingerprint:
'''
$ step ca bootstrap --ca-url https://ca.example.com \
  --fingerprint d9d0978692f1c7cc791f5c343ce98771900721405e834cd27b9502cc719f5097
'''

Bootstrap and install the root certificate
'''
$ step ca bootstrap --ca-url https://ca.example.com \
  --fingerprint d9d0978692f1c7cc791f5c343ce98771900721405e834cd27b9502cc719f5097 \
  --install
'''

Bootstrap with a smallstep.com CA using a team ID:
'''
$ step ca bootstrap --team superteam
'''

To use team IDs in your own environment, you'll need an HTTP(S) server
serving a JSON file:
'''
{"url":"https://ca.example.com","fingerprint":"d9d0978692f1c7cc791f5c343ce98771900721405e834cd27b9502cc719f5097"}
'''

Then, this command will look for the file at https://config.example.com/superteam:
'''
$ step ca bootstrap --team superteam --team-url https://config.example.com/<>
'''`,
		Flags: []cli.Flag{
			flags.CaURL,
			fingerprintFlag,
			cli.BoolFlag{
				Name:  "install",
				Usage: "Install the root certificate into the system's default trust store.",
			},
			flags.Team,
			flags.TeamAuthority,
			flags.TeamURL,
			flags.RedirectURL,
			flags.Force,
			flags.Context,
			flags.ContextProfile,
			flags.ContextAuthority,
			flags.HiddenNoContext,
		},
	}
}

func bootstrapAction(ctx *cli.Context) error {
	caURL, err := flags.ParseCaURLIfExists(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	fingerprint := strings.TrimSpace(ctx.String("fingerprint"))
	team := ctx.String("team")
	teamAuthority := ctx.String("team-authority")

	switch {
	case team != "" && caURL != "":
		return errs.IncompatibleFlagWithFlag(ctx, "team", "ca-url")
	case team != "" && fingerprint != "":
		return errs.IncompatibleFlagWithFlag(ctx, "team", "fingerprint")
	case team != "" && teamAuthority != "":
		return cautils.BootstrapTeamAuthority(ctx, team, teamAuthority)
	case team != "":
		return cautils.BootstrapTeamAuthority(ctx, team, "ssh")
	case teamAuthority != "":
		return errs.RequiredWithFlag(ctx, "team-authority", "team")
	case caURL == "":
		return errs.RequiredFlag(ctx, "ca-url")
	case fingerprint == "":
		return errs.RequiredFlag(ctx, "fingerprint")
	default:
		return cautils.BootstrapAuthority(ctx, caURL, fingerprint)
	}
}

45: Provisioning credentials are simple JWK key pairs using public-key cryptography.
46: The public key is used to verify a provisioning token while the private key is

51: Each provisioner is able to manage a different set of rules that can be used to
52: configure the bounds of the certificate.

58:   practice is to use an email address for this.

62:   used to sign the provisioning tokens.

105: func newCRUDClient(cliCtx *cli.Context, cfgFile string) (crudClient, error) {
106: 	unauthAdminClient, err := cautils.NewUnauthenticatedAdminClient(cliCtx)
107: 	if err != nil {
108: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("error generating admin client: %w", err)
109: 	}
110: 
111: 	var netErr *net.OpError
112: 
113: 	err = unauthAdminClient.IsEnabled()
114: 	switch {
115: 	case errors.As(err, &netErr) || errors.Is(err, ca.ErrAdminAPINotImplemented):
116: 		ui.PrintSelected("CA Configuration", cfgFile)
117: 		cfg, err := config.LoadConfiguration(cfgFile)
118: 		if err != nil {
119: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("error loading configuration: %w", err)
120: 		}
121: 		// Assume the ca.json is already valid to avoid enabling all the
122: 		// features present in step-ca just to modify the provisioners.
123: 		cfg.SkipValidation = true
124: 
125: 		ui.Println()
126: 		return newCaConfigClient(context.Background(), cfg, cfgFile)
127: 	case errors.Is(err, ca.ErrAdminAPINotAuthorized):
128: 		return cautils.NewAdminClient(cliCtx)
129: 	default:
130: 		return nil, err
131: 	}
132: }

134: func parseInstanceAge(ctx *cli.Context) (age string, err error) {
135: 	if !ctx.IsSet("instance-age") {
136: 		return
137: 	}
138: 	age = ctx.String("instance-age")
139: 	dur, err := time.ParseDuration(age)
140: 	if err != nil {
141: 		return "", err
142: 	}
143: 	if dur < 0 {
144: 		return "", errs.MinSizeFlag(ctx, "instance-age", "0s")
145: 	}
146: 	return
147: }

149: func removeElements(list, rems []string) []string {
150: 	if len(list) == 0 {
151: 		return list
152: 	}
153: 	for _, rem := range rems {
154: 		for i, elem := range list {
155: 			if elem == rem {
156: 				list[i] = list[len(list)-1]
157: 				list = list[:len(list)-1]
158: 				break
159: 			}
160: 		}
161: 	}
162: 	return list
163: }

652: 	}

656: 	for len(b) > 0 {

660: 		}
661: 		if crt.IsCA() {

663: 		}
664: 	}

667: 	}

670: 	for i, crt := range certs {
671: 		b, err = crt.MarshalPEM()
672: 		if err != nil {
673: 			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "error marshaling certificate")
674: 		}
675: 		rootBytes[i] = b
676: 	}
677:

# Run `make bootstrap` to set up your local environment.
# To build using go, use `make build`
# For a binary that's in parity with how our CI system builds,
# run `make goreleaser` to build using GoReleaser Pro.

# Variables:
# V=1 for verbose output.

# the name of the executable
BINNAME?=step

# the build output path
PREFIX?=bin

# the install path
DESTDIR?=/usr/local/bin

# GOOS_OVERRIDE="GOOS=linux GOARCH=arm GOARM=6" to change OS and arch
GOOS_OVERRIDE?=

# CGO_OVERRIDE="CGO_ENABLED=1" to enable CGO
CGO_OVERRIDE?=CGO_ENABLED=0

# which build id in .goreleaser.yml to build
GORELEASER_BUILD_ID?=default

# all go files
SRC=$(shell find . -type f -name '*.go' -or -name go.mod -or -name go.sum)

all: lint test build

ci: test build

.PHONY: all ci

#################################################
# Determine the type of `push` and `version`
#################################################

ifdef GITHUB_REF
VERSION ?= $(shell echo $(GITHUB_REF) | sed 's/^refs\/tags\///')
NOT_RC  := $(shell echo $(VERSION) | grep -v -e -rc)
	ifeq ($(NOT_RC),)
PUSHTYPE := release-candidate
	else
PUSHTYPE := release
	endif
else
VERSION ?= $(shell [ -d .git ] && git describe --tags --always --dirty="-dev")
# If we are not in an active git dir then try reading the version from .VERSION.
# .VERSION contains a slug populated by `git archive`.
VERSION := $(or $(VERSION),$(shell make/version.sh .VERSION))
PUSHTYPE := branch
endif

VERSION := $(shell echo $(VERSION) | sed 's/^v//')

ifdef V
$(info    GITHUB_REF is $(GITHUB_REF))
$(info    VERSION is $(VERSION))
$(info    PUSHTYPE is $(PUSHTYPE))
endif

DATE    := $(shell date -u '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M UTC')
ifdef DEBUG
	LDFLAGS := -ldflags='-X "main.Version=$(VERSION)" -X "main.BuildTime=$(DATE)"'
	GCFLAGS := -gcflags "all=-N -l"
else
	LDFLAGS := -ldflags='-w -X "main.Version=$(VERSION)" -X "main.BuildTime=$(DATE)"'
	GCFLAGS :=
endif

Q=$(if $V,,@)
OUTPUT_ROOT=output/

ifeq ($(OS),Windows_NT)
	HOSTOS=Windows
else
	HOSTOS=$(shell uname)
endif

HOSTARCH=$(shell go env GOHOSTARCH)
ifeq ($(HOSTARCH),amd64)
       HOSTARCH=x86_64
endif

GORELEASER_PRO_URL=https://github.com/goreleaser/goreleaser-pro/releases/latest/download/goreleaser-pro_$(HOSTOS)_$(HOSTARCH).tar.gz

# Determine the hooks to skip. When using GoReleaser OSS with a Pro config, specifying "after"
# to be skipped results in an error. When using GoReleaser Pro running the "goreleaser-local"
# target both "post-hooks" and "after" are required to skip the upload to GCP. The logic below 
# checks the GoReleaser binary to be Pro or not, and then sets the steps to skip accordingly. 
# It's possible this is a GoReleaser bug for the case where a Pro config is used with GoReleaser 
# OSS.
GORELEASER_OSS_SKIP=post-hooks
GORELEASER_PRO_SKIP=post-hooks,after
GORELEASER_SKIP=$(if $(filter true,$(shell goreleaser --version | grep -q goreleaser-pro && echo true || echo false)),$(GORELEASER_PRO_SKIP),$(GORELEASER_OSS_SKIP))

.PHONY: all

#########################################
# Bootstrapping
#########################################
TMPDIR := $(shell mktemp -d)
bootstra%: GOPATH=$(shell go env GOPATH)
bootstra%:
	$Q curl -sSfL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/golangci/golangci-lint/master/install.sh | sh -s -- -b $$(go env GOPATH)/bin latest
	$Q go install golang.org/x/vuln/cmd/govulncheck@latest
	$Q go install gotest.tools/gotestsum@latest
	$Q go install golang.org/x/tools/cmd/goimports@latest
	@echo "Installing GoReleaser Pro into $(GOPATH)/bin"
	$Q curl -o $(TMPDIR)/goreleaser.tar.gz -L $(GORELEASER_PRO_URL)
	$Q ls $(TMPDIR)
	$Q tar xvzf $(TMPDIR)/goreleaser.tar.gz -C $(TMPDIR)
	$Q cp $(TMPDIR)/goreleaser $(GOPATH)/bin

.PHONY: bootstra%

#########################################
# Build
#########################################

build: $(PREFIX)/$(BINNAME)
	@echo "Build Complete!"

$(PREFIX)/$(BINNAME): $(SRC)
	$Q mkdir -p $(PREFIX)
	$Q $(GOOS_OVERRIDE) $(CGO_OVERRIDE) go build \
		-v \
	   	-o $(PREFIX)/$(BINNAME) \
		$(GCFLAGS) $(LDFLAGS) \
	   	github.com/smallstep/cli/cmd/step

goreleaser:
	$Q mkdir -p $(PREFIX)
	$Q $(GOOS_OVERRIDE) $(CGO_OVERRIDE) DEBUG=$(DEBUG) goreleaser build \
		--id $(GORELEASER_BUILD_ID) \
	   	--snapshot \
		--single-target \
	   	--clean \
		--skip=$(GORELEASER_SKIP) \
		--output $(PREFIX)/$(BINNAME)

.PHONY: build goreleaser


#########################################
# Test
#########################################

test:
	$Q $(CGO_OVERRIDE) $(GOFLAGS) gotestsum -- -coverprofile=coverage.out -short -covermode=atomic ./...

race:
	$Q $(CGO_OVERRIDE) $(GOFLAGS) gotestsum -- -race ./...

.PHONY: test race

#########################################
# Linting
#########################################

fmt:
	$Q goimports -local github.com/golangci/golangci-lint -l -w $(SRC)

lint: golint govulncheck

golint: SHELL:=/bin/bash
golint:
	$Q LOG_LEVEL=error golangci-lint run --config <(curl -s https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallstep/workflows/master/.golangci.yml) --timeout=30m

govulncheck:
	$Q govulncheck ./...

.PHONY: fmt lint golint govulncheck

#########################################
# Install
#########################################

install: $(PREFIX)/$(BINNAME)
	$Q mkdir -p $(DESTDIR)/
	$Q install $(PREFIX)/$(BINNAME) $(DESTDIR)/$(BINNAME)

uninstall:
	$Q rm -f $(DESTDIR)/$(BINNAME)

.PHONY: install uninstall

#########################################
# Clean
#########################################

clean:
	$Q rm -f $(PREFIX)/$(BINNAME)
	$Q rm -rf dist

.PHONY: clean

#################################################
# Build statically compiled step binary for various operating systems
#################################################

BINARY_OUTPUT=$(OUTPUT_ROOT)binary/

define BUNDLE_MAKE
	# $(1) -- Go Operating System (e.g. linux, darwin, windows, etc.)
	# $(2) -- Go Architecture (e.g. amd64, arm, arm64, etc.)
	# $(3) -- Go ARM architectural family (e.g. 7, 8, etc.)
	# $(4) -- Parent directory for executables generated by 'make'.
	$Q GOOS_OVERRIDE='GOOS=$(1) GOARCH=$(2) GOARM=$(3)' PREFIX=$(4) make $(4)/$(BINNAME)
endef

binary-linux-amd64:
	$(call BUNDLE_MAKE,linux,amd64,,$(BINARY_OUTPUT)linux-amd64)

binary-linux-arm64:
	$(call BUNDLE_MAKE,linux,arm64,,$(BINARY_OUTPUT)linux-arm64)

binary-linux-armv7:
	$(call BUNDLE_MAKE,linux,arm,7,$(BINARY_OUTPUT)linux-armv7)

binary-linux-mips:
	$(call BUNDLE_MAKE,linux,mips,,$(BINARY_OUTPUT)linux-mips)

binary-darwin-amd64:
	$(call BUNDLE_MAKE,darwin,amd64,,$(BINARY_OUTPUT)darwin-amd64)

binary-darwin-arm64:
	$(call BUNDLE_MAKE,darwin,arm64,,$(BINARY_OUTPUT)darwin-arm64)

binary-windows-amd64:
	$(call BUNDLE_MAKE,windows,amd64,,$(BINARY_OUTPUT)windows-amd64)

.PHONY: binary-linux-amd64 binary-linux-arm64 binary-linux-armv7 binary-linux-mips binary-darwin-amd64 binary-darwin-arm64 binary-windows-amd64

44: 	return cli.Command{
45: 		Name:   "renew",
46: 		Action: command.ActionFunc(renewCertificateAction),
47: 		Usage:  "renew a certificate",
48: 		UsageText: `**step ca renew** <crt-file> <key-file>
49: [**--mtls**] [**--password-file**=<file>] [**--out**=<file>] [**--expires-in**=<duration>]
50: [**--force**] [**--pid**=<int>] [**--pid-file**=<file>] [**--signal**=<int>]
51: [**--exec**=<string>] [**--daemon**] [**--renew-period**=<duration>] [**--kms**=<uri>]
52: [**--ca-url**=<uri>] [**--root**=<file>] [**--context**=<name>]`,
53: 		Description: `
54: **step ca renew** command renews the given certificate (with a request to the
55: certificate authority) and writes the new certificate to disk - either overwriting
56: <crt-file> or using a new file when the **--out**=<file> flag is used.
57: 
58: With the **--daemon** flag the command will periodically update the given
59: certificate. By default, it will renew the certificate before 2/3 of the validity
60: period of the certificate has elapsed. A random jitter is used to avoid multiple
61: instances running at the same time. The amount of time between renewal and
62: certificate expiration can be configured using the **--expires-in** flag, or a
63: fixed period can be set with the **--renew-period** flag.
64: 
65: The **--daemon** flag can be combined with **--pid**, **--signal**, or **--exec**
66: to provide certificate reloads on your services.
67: 
68: By default, the renew command authenticates to step-ca using mTLS, except when
69: the certificate is expired and renewal after expiry is allowed by the CA.
70: 
71: There are scenarios where mTLS is not possible: When step-ca is behind a layer 7 proxy,
72: when the server's leaf certificate EKU is not configured for client authentication,
73: or when the server is a StepCAS RA for an upstream step-ca server.
74: For these scenarios, use **--mtls=false** to force a flow that uses X5C
75: token-based authentication.
76: 
77: ## POSITIONAL ARGUMENTS
78: 
79: <crt-file>
80: :  The certificate in PEM format that we want to renew.
81: 
82: <key-file>
83: :  They key file of the certificate.
84: 
85: ## EXAMPLES
86: 
87: Renew a certificate with the configured CA:
88: '''
89: $ step ca renew internal.crt internal.key
90: Would you like to overwrite internal.crt [Y/n]: y
91: '''
92: 
93: Renew a certificate without overwriting the previous certificate:
94: '''
95: $ step ca renew --out renewed.crt internal.crt internal.key
96: '''
97: 
98: Renew a certificate forcing the overwrite of the previous certificate:
99: '''
100: $ step ca renew --force internal.crt internal.key
101: '''
102: 
103: Renew a certificate using the token flow instead of mTLS:
104: '''
105: $ step ca renew --mtls=false --force internal.crt internal.key
106: '''
107: 
108: Renew a certificate which key is in a KMS:
109: '''
110: $ step ca renew yubikey.crt 'yubikey:slot-id=9a?pin-value=123456'
111: '''
112: 
113: Renew a certificate which key is in a KMS, using the <--kms> flag:
114: '''
115: $ step ca renew \
116:   --kms 'pkcs11:module-path=/usr/local/lib/softhsm/libsofthsm2.so;token=smallstep?pin-value=password' \
117:   pkcs11.crt 'pkcs11:id=4001'
118: '''
119: 
120: Renew a certificate providing the <--ca-url> and <--root> flags:
121: '''
122: $ step ca renew --ca-url https://ca.smallstep.com:9000 \
123:   --root /path/to/root_ca.crt internal.crt internal.key
124: Would you like to overwrite internal.crt [Y/n]: y
125: '''
126: 
127: Renew skipped because it was too early:
128: '''
129: $ step ca renew --expires-in 8h internal.crt internal.key
130: certificate not renewed: expires in 10h52m5s
131: '''
132: 
133: Renew the certificate before 2/3 of the validity has passed:
134: '''
135: $ step ca renew --daemon internal.crt internal.key
136: '''
137: 
138: Renew the certificate before 8 hours and 30m of the expiration time:
139: '''
140: $ step ca renew --daemon --expires-in 8h30m internal.crt internal.key
141: '''
142: 
143: Renew the certificate every 16h:
144: '''
145: $ step ca renew --daemon --renew-period 16h internal.crt internal.key
146: '''
147: 
148: Renew the certificate and reload nginx:
149: '''
150: $ step ca renew --daemon --exec "nginx -s reload" internal.crt internal.key
151: '''
152: 
153: Renew the certificate and convert it to DER:
154: '''
155: $ step ca renew --daemon --renew-period 16h \
156:   --exec "step certificate format --force --out internal.der internal.crt" \
157:   internal.crt internal.key
158: '''
159: 
160: Renew a certificate using the offline mode, requires the configuration
161: files, certificates, and keys created with **step ca init**:
162: '''
163: $ step ca renew --offline internal.crt internal.key
164: '''`,
165: 		Flags: []cli.Flag{
166: 			cli.BoolTFlag{
167: 				Name: "mtls",
168: 				Usage: `Use mTLS to renew a certificate. Use --mtls=false to force the token
169: authorization flow instead.`,
170: 			},
171: 			flags.CaConfig,
172: 			flags.Force,
173: 			flags.Offline,
174: 			flags.PasswordFile,
175: 			flags.KMSUri,
176: 			cli.StringFlag{
177: 				Name:  "out,output-file",
178: 				Usage: "The new certificate <file> path. Defaults to overwriting the <crt-file> positional argument",
179: 			},
180: 			cli.StringFlag{
181: 				Name: "expires-in",
182: 				Usage: `The amount of time remaining before certificate expiration,
183: at which point a renewal should be attempted. The certificate renewal will not
184: be performed if the time to expiration is greater than the **--expires-in** value.
185: A random jitter (duration/20) will be added to avoid multiple services hitting the
186: renew endpoint at the same time. The <duration> is a sequence of decimal numbers,
187: each with optional fraction and a unit suffix, such as "300ms", "-1.5h" or "2h45m".
188: Valid time units are "ns", "us" (or "µs"), "ms", "s", "m", "h".`,
189: 			},
190: 			cli.IntFlag{
191: 				Name: "pid",
192: 				Usage: `The process id to signal after the certificate has been renewed. By default the
193: the SIGHUP (1) signal will be used, but this can be configured with the **--signal**
194: flag.`,
195: 			},
196: 			cli.StringFlag{
197: 				Name: "pid-file",
198: 				Usage: `The <file> from which to read the process id that will be signaled after the certificate
199: has been renewed. By default the SIGHUP (1) signal will be used, but this can be configured with the **--signal**
200: flag.`,
201: 			},
202: 			cli.IntFlag{
203: 				Name: "signal",
204: 				Usage: `The signal <number> to send to the selected PID, so it can reload the
205: configuration and load the new certificate. Default value is SIGHUP (1)`,
206: 				Value: int(syscall.SIGHUP),
207: 			},
208: 			cli.StringFlag{
209: 				Name:  "exec",
210: 				Usage: "The <command> to run after the certificate has been renewed.",
211: 			},
212: 			cli.BoolFlag{
213: 				Name: "daemon",
214: 				Usage: `Run the renew command as a daemon, renewing and overwriting the certificate
215: periodically. By default the daemon will renew a certificate before 2/3 of the
216: time to expiration has elapsed. The period can be configured using the
217: **--renew-period** or **--expires-in** flags.`,
218: 			},
219: 			cli.StringFlag{
220: 				Name: "renew-period",
221: 				Usage: `The period with which to schedule renewals of the certificate in daemon mode.
222: Requires the **--daemon** flag. The <duration> is a sequence of decimal numbers,
223: each with optional fraction and a unit suffix, such as "300ms", "1.5h", or "2h45m".
224: Valid time units are "ns", "us" (or "µs"), "ms", "s", "m", "h".`,
225: 			},
226: 			flags.CaURL,
227: 			flags.Root,
228: 			flags.Context,
229: 		},
230: 	}
231: }

233: func renewCertificateAction(ctx *cli.Context) error {
234: 	err := errs.NumberOfArguments(ctx, 2)
235: 	if err != nil {
236: 		return err
237: 	}
238: 
239: 	args := ctx.Args()
240: 	certFile := args.Get(0)
241: 	keyFile := args.Get(1)
242: 	passFile := ctx.String("password-file")
243: 	isDaemon := ctx.Bool("daemon")
244: 	execCmd := ctx.String("exec")
245: 	kmsURI := ctx.String("kms")
246: 
247: 	outFile := ctx.String("out")
248: 	if outFile == "" {
249: 		outFile = certFile
250: 	}
251: 
252: 	rootFile := ctx.String("root")
253: 	if rootFile == "" {
254: 		rootFile = pki.GetRootCAPath()
255: 	}
256: 
257: 	caURL, err := flags.ParseCaURL(ctx)
258: 	if err != nil {
259: 		return err
260: 	}
261: 
262: 	var expiresIn, renewPeriod time.Duration
263: 	if s := ctx.String("expires-in"); s != "" {
264: 		if expiresIn, err = time.ParseDuration(s); err != nil {
265: 			return errs.InvalidFlagValue(ctx, "expires-in", s, "")
266: 		}
267: 	}
268: 	if s := ctx.String("renew-period"); s != "" {
269: 		if renewPeriod, err = time.ParseDuration(s); err != nil {
270: 			return errs.InvalidFlagValue(ctx, "renew-period", s, "")
271: 		}
272: 	}
273: 	if expiresIn > 0 && renewPeriod > 0 {
274: 		return errs.IncompatibleFlagWithFlag(ctx, "expires-in", "renew-period")
275: 	}
276: 	if renewPeriod > 0 && !isDaemon {
277: 		return errs.RequiredWithFlag(ctx, "renew-period", "daemon")
278: 	}
279: 
280: 	if ctx.IsSet("pid") && ctx.IsSet("pid-file") {
281: 		return errs.MutuallyExclusiveFlags(ctx, "pid", "pid-file")
282: 	}
283: 	pid := ctx.Int("pid")
284: 	if ctx.IsSet("pid") && pid <= 0 {
285: 		return errs.InvalidFlagValue(ctx, "pid", strconv.Itoa(pid), "")
286: 	}
287: 
288: 	pidFile := ctx.String("pid-file")
289: 	if pidFile != "" {
290: 		pidB, err := os.ReadFile(pidFile)
291: 		if err != nil {
292: 			return errs.FileError(err, pidFile)
293: 		}
294: 		pid, err = strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimSpace(string(pidB)))
295: 		if err != nil {
296: 			return errs.Wrap(err, "error converting %s to integer process id", pidB)
297: 		}
298: 		if pid <= 0 {
299: 			return errs.InvalidFlagValue(ctx, "pid-file", strconv.Itoa(pid), "")
300: 		}
301: 	}
302: 
303: 	signum := ctx.Int("signal")
304: 	if ctx.IsSet("signal") && signum <= 0 {
305: 		return errs.InvalidFlagValue(ctx, "signal", strconv.Itoa(signum), "")
306: 	}
307: 
308: 	cert, err := tlsLoadX509KeyPair(kmsURI, certFile, keyFile, passFile)
309: 	if err != nil {
310: 		return err
311: 	}
312: 
313: 	cvp := cert.Leaf.NotAfter.Sub(cert.Leaf.NotBefore)
314: 	if renewPeriod > 0 && renewPeriod >= cvp {
315: 		return errors.Errorf("flag '--renew-period' must be within (lower than) the certificate "+
316: 			"validity period; renew-period=%v, cert-validity-period=%v", renewPeriod, cvp)
317: 	}
318: 	if expiresIn > cvp {
319: 		return errors.Errorf("flag '--expires-in' must be within (lower than) the certificate "+
320: 			"validity period; expires-in=%v, cert-validity-period=%v", expiresIn, cvp)
321: 	}
322: 
323: 	renewer, err := newRenewer(ctx, caURL, cert, rootFile)
324: 	if err != nil {
325: 		return err
326: 	}
327: 
328: 	afterRenew := getAfterRenewFunc(pid, signum, execCmd)
329: 	if isDaemon {
330: 		// Force is always enabled when daemon mode is used
331: 		ctx.Set("force", "true")
332: 		next := nextRenewDuration(cert.Leaf, expiresIn, renewPeriod)
333: 		return renewer.Daemon(outFile, next, expiresIn, renewPeriod, afterRenew)
334: 	}
335: 
336: 	// Do not renew if (cert.notAfter - now) > (expiresIn + jitter)
337: 	if expiresIn > 0 {
338: 		//nolint:gosec // The random number below is not being used for crypto.
339: 		jitter := rand.Int63n(int64(expiresIn / 20))
340: 		if d := time.Until(cert.Leaf.NotAfter); d > expiresIn+time.Duration(jitter) {
341: 			ui.Printf("certificate not renewed: expires in %s\n", d.Round(time.Second))
342: 			return nil
343: 		}
344: 	}
345: 
346: 	if _, err := renewer.Renew(outFile); err != nil {
347: 		return err
348: 	}
349: 
350: 	ui.Printf("Your certificate has been saved in %s.\n", outFile)
351: 	return afterRenew()
352: }
353: 
354: func nextRenewDuration(leaf *x509.Certificate, expiresIn, renewPeriod time.Duration) time.Duration {
355: 	if renewPeriod > 0 {
356: 		// Renew now if it will be expired in renewPeriod
357: 		if (time.Until(leaf.NotAfter) - renewPeriod) <= 0 {
358: 			return 0
359: 		}
360: 		return renewPeriod
361: 	}
362: 
363: 	period := leaf.NotAfter.Sub(leaf.NotBefore)
364: 	if expiresIn == 0 {
365: 		expiresIn = period / 3
366: 	}
367: 
368: 	switch d := time.Until(leaf.NotAfter) - expiresIn; {
369: 	case d <= 0:
370: 		return 0
371: 	case d < period/20:
372: 		//nolint:gosec // The random number below is not being used for crypto.
373: 		return time.Duration(rand.Int63n(int64(d)))
374: 	default:
375: 		//nolint:gosec // The random number below is not being used for crypto.
376: 		n := rand.Int63n(int64(period / 20))
377: 		d -= time.Duration(n)
378: 		return d
379: 	}
380: }

382: func getAfterRenewFunc(pid, signum int, execCmd string) func() error {
383: 	return func() error {
384: 		if err := runKillPid(pid, signum); err != nil {
385: 			return err
386: 		}
387: 		return runExecCmd(execCmd)
388: 	}
389: }
390: 
391: func runKillPid(pid, signum int) error {
392: 	if pid == 0 {
393: 		return nil
394: 	}
395: 	if err := sysutils.Kill(pid, syscall.Signal(signum)); err != nil {
396: 		return errors.Wrapf(err, "kill %d with signal %d failed", pid, signum)
397: 	}
398: 	return nil
399: }
400: 
401: func runExecCmd(execCmd string) error {
402: 	execCmd = strings.TrimSpace(execCmd)
403: 	if execCmd == "" {
404: 		return nil
405: 	}
406: 	parts := strings.Split(execCmd, " ")
407: 	//nolint:gosec // arguments controlled by step.
408: 	cmd := exec.Command(parts[0], parts[1:]...)
409: 	cmd.Stdin = os.Stdin
410: 	cmd.Stdout = os.Stdout
411: 	cmd.Stderr = os.Stderr
412: 	return cmd.Run()
413: }

415: type renewer struct {
416: 	client    cautils.CaClient
417: 	transport *http.Transport
418: 	key       crypto.PrivateKey
419: 	offline   bool
420: 	cert      tls.Certificate
421: 	caURL     *url.URL
422: 	mtls      bool
423: }
424: 
425: func newRenewer(ctx *cli.Context, caURL string, cert tls.Certificate, rootFile string) (*renewer, error) {
426: 	if len(cert.Certificate) == 0 {
427: 		return nil, errors.New("error loading certificate: certificate chain is empty")
428: 	}
429: 
430: 	rootCAs, err := x509util.ReadCertPool(rootFile)
431: 	if err != nil {
432: 		return nil, err
433: 	}
434: 
435: 	tr := &http.Transport{
436: 		Proxy: http.ProxyFromEnvironment,
437: 		TLSClientConfig: &tls.Config{
438: 			RootCAs:                  rootCAs,
439: 			PreferServerCipherSuites: true,
440: 			MinVersion:               tls.VersionTLS12,
441: 		},
442: 	}
443: 
444: 	if time.Now().Before(cert.Leaf.NotAfter) {
445: 		tr.TLSClientConfig.Certificates = []tls.Certificate{cert}
446: 	}
447: 
448: 	var client cautils.CaClient
449: 	offline := ctx.Bool("offline")
450: 	if offline {
451: 		caConfig := ctx.String("ca-config")
452: 		if caConfig == "" {
453: 			return nil, errs.InvalidFlagValue(ctx, "ca-config", "", "")
454: 		}
455: 		client, err = cautils.NewOfflineCA(ctx, caConfig)
456: 		if err != nil {
457: 			return nil, err
458: 		}
459: 	} else {
460: 		client, err = ca.NewClient(caURL, ca.WithTransport(tr))
461: 		if err != nil {
462: 			return nil, err
463: 		}
464: 	}
465: 
466: 	u, err := url.Parse(client.GetCaURL())
467: 	if err != nil {
468: 		return nil, errors.Errorf("error parsing CA URL: %s", client.GetCaURL())
469: 	}
470: 
471: 	return &renewer{
472: 		client:    client,
473: 		transport: tr,
474: 		key:       cert.PrivateKey,
475: 		offline:   offline,
476: 		cert:      cert,
477: 		caURL:     u,
478: 		mtls:      ctx.Bool("mtls"),
479: 	}, nil
480: }
481: 
482: func (r *renewer) Renew(outFile string) (resp *api.SignResponse, err error) {
483: 	if !r.mtls || time.Now().After(r.cert.Leaf.NotAfter) {
484: 		resp, err = r.RenewWithToken(r.cert)
485: 	} else {
486: 		resp, err = r.client.Renew(r.transport)
487: 	}
488: 	if err != nil {
489: 		return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "error renewing certificate")
490: 	}
491: 
492: 	if len(resp.CertChainPEM) == 0 {
493: 		resp.CertChainPEM = []api.Certificate{resp.ServerPEM, resp.CaPEM}
494: 	}
495: 	var data []byte
496: 	for _, certPEM := range resp.CertChainPEM {
497: 		pemblk, err := pemutil.Serialize(certPEM.Certificate)
498: 		if err != nil {
499: 			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "error serializing certificate PEM")
500: 		}
501: 		data = append(data, pem.EncodeToMemory(pemblk)...)
502: 	}
503: 	if err := fileutil.WriteFile(outFile, data, 0o600); err != nil {
504: 		return nil, errs.FileError(err, outFile)
505: 	}
506: 
507: 	return resp, nil
508: }

510: func (r *renewer) Rekey(priv interface{}, outCert, outKey string, writePrivateKey bool) (*api.SignResponse, error) {
511: 	csrBytes, err := x509.CreateCertificateRequest(cryptoRand.Reader, &x509.CertificateRequest{}, priv)
512: 	if err != nil {
513: 		return nil, err
514: 	}
515: 	csr, err := x509.ParseCertificateRequest(csrBytes)
516: 	if err != nil {
517: 		return nil, err
518: 	}
519: 	resp, err := r.client.Rekey(&api.RekeyRequest{CsrPEM: api.NewCertificateRequest(csr)}, r.transport)
520: 	if err != nil {
521: 		return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "error rekeying certificate")
522: 	}
523: 	if len(resp.CertChainPEM) == 0 {
524: 		resp.CertChainPEM = []api.Certificate{resp.ServerPEM, resp.CaPEM}
525: 	}
526: 	var data []byte
527: 	for _, certPEM := range resp.CertChainPEM {
528: 		pemblk, err := pemutil.Serialize(certPEM.Certificate)
529: 		if err != nil {
530: 			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "error serializing certificate PEM")
531: 		}
532: 		data = append(data, pem.EncodeToMemory(pemblk)...)
533: 	}
534: 	if err := fileutil.WriteFile(outCert, data, 0o600); err != nil {
535: 		return nil, errs.FileError(err, outCert)
536: 	}
537: 	if writePrivateKey {
538: 		_, err = pemutil.Serialize(priv, pemutil.ToFile(outKey, 0o600))
539: 		if err != nil {
540: 			return nil, err
541: 		}
542: 	}
543: 
544: 	return resp, nil
545: }

547: // RenewAndPrepareNext renews the cert and prepares the cert for it's next renewal.
548: // NOTE: this function logs each time the certificate is successfully renewed.
549: func (r *renewer) RenewAndPrepareNext(outFile string, expiresIn, renewPeriod time.Duration) (time.Duration, error) {
550: 	const durationOnErrors = 1 * time.Minute
551: 	infoLog := log.New(os.Stdout, "INFO: ", log.LstdFlags)
552: 
553: 	resp, err := r.Renew(outFile)
554: 	if err != nil {
555: 		return durationOnErrors, err
556: 	}
557: 
558: 	x509Chain, err := pemutil.ReadCertificateBundle(outFile)
559: 	if err != nil {
560: 		return durationOnErrors, errs.Wrap(err, "error reading certificate chain")
561: 	}
562: 	x509ChainBytes := make([][]byte, len(x509Chain))
563: 	for i, c := range x509Chain {
564: 		x509ChainBytes[i] = c.Raw
565: 	}
566: 
567: 	cert := tls.Certificate{
568: 		Certificate: x509ChainBytes,
569: 		PrivateKey:  r.key,
570: 		Leaf:        x509Chain[0],
571: 	}
572: 	if len(cert.Certificate) == 0 {
573: 		return durationOnErrors, errors.New("error loading certificate: certificate chain is empty")
574: 	}
575: 
576: 	// Prepare next transport
577: 	r.cert = cert
578: 	r.transport.TLSClientConfig.Certificates = []tls.Certificate{cert}
579: 
580: 	// Get next renew duration
581: 	next := nextRenewDuration(resp.ServerPEM.Certificate, expiresIn, renewPeriod)
582: 	infoLog.Printf("%s certificate renewed, next in %s", resp.ServerPEM.Certificate.Subject.CommonName, next.Round(time.Second))
583: 	return next, nil
584: }
585: 
586: func (r *renewer) Daemon(outFile string, next, expiresIn, renewPeriod time.Duration, afterRenew func() error) error {
587: 	// Loggers
588: 	infoLog := log.New(os.Stdout, "INFO: ", log.LstdFlags)
589: 	errLog := log.New(os.Stderr, "ERROR: ", log.LstdFlags)
590: 
591: 	// Daemon loop
592: 	signals := make(chan os.Signal, 1)
593: 	signal.Notify(signals, syscall.SIGINT, syscall.SIGTERM, syscall.SIGHUP)
594: 	defer signal.Stop(signals)
595: 
596: 	infoLog.Printf("first renewal in %s", next.Round(time.Second))
597: 	var err error
598: 	for {
599: 		select {
600: 		case sig := <-signals:
601: 			switch sig {
602: 			case syscall.SIGHUP:
603: 				if next, err = r.RenewAndPrepareNext(outFile, expiresIn, renewPeriod); err != nil {
604: 					errLog.Println(err)
605: 				} else if err := afterRenew(); err != nil {
606: 					errLog.Println(err)
607: 				}
608: 			case syscall.SIGINT, syscall.SIGTERM:
609: 				return nil
610: 			}
611: 		case <-time.After(next):
612: 			if next, err = r.RenewAndPrepareNext(outFile, expiresIn, renewPeriod); err != nil {
613: 				errLog.Println(err)
614: 			} else if err := afterRenew(); err != nil {
615: 				errLog.Println(err)
616: 			}
617: 		}
618: 	}
619: }

621: // RenewWithToken creates an authorization token with the given certificate and
622: // attempts to renew the given certificate. It can be used to renew expired
623: // certificates.
624: func (r *renewer) RenewWithToken(cert tls.Certificate) (*api.SignResponse, error) {
625: 	claims, err := token.NewClaims(
626: 		token.WithAudience(r.caURL.ResolveReference(&url.URL{Path: "/renew"}).String()),
627: 		token.WithIssuer("step-ca-client/1.0"),
628: 		token.WithSubject(cert.Leaf.Subject.CommonName),
629: 	)
630: 	if err != nil {
631: 		return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "error creating authorization token")
632: 	}
633: 	var x5c []string
634: 	for _, b := range cert.Certificate {
635: 		x5c = append(x5c, base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(b))
636: 	}
637: 	if claims.ExtraHeaders == nil {
638: 		claims.ExtraHeaders = make(map[string]interface{})
639: 	}
640: 	claims.ExtraHeaders[jose.X5cInsecureKey] = x5c
641: 
642: 	tok, err := claims.Sign("", cert.PrivateKey)
643: 	if err != nil {
644: 		return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "error signing authorization token")
645: 	}
646: 
647: 	// Remove existing certificate from the transport. And close keep-alive
648: 	// connections. When daemon is used we don't want to re-use the connection
649: 	// that did not include a certificate.
650: 	r.transport.TLSClientConfig.Certificates = nil
651: 	defer r.transport.CloseIdleConnections()
652: 
653: 	return r.client.RenewWithToken(tok)
654: }

657: 	x509Chain, err := pemutil.ReadCertificateBundle(certFile)
658: 	if err != nil {
659: 		return tls.Certificate{}, errs.Wrap(err, "error reading certificate chain")
660: 	}
661: 	x509ChainBytes := make([][]byte, len(x509Chain))
662: 	for i, c := range x509Chain {
663: 		x509ChainBytes[i] = c.Raw
664: 	}
665: 
666: 	opts := []pemutil.Options{pemutil.WithFilename(keyFile)}
667: 	if passFile != "" {
668: 		opts = append(opts, pemutil.WithPasswordFile(passFile))
669: 	}
670: 	signer, err := cryptoutil.CreateSigner(kms, keyFile, opts...)
671: 	if err != nil {
672: 		return tls.Certificate{}, errs.Wrap(err, "error loading private key")
673: 	}
674: 	return tls.Certificate{
675: 		Certificate: x509ChainBytes,
676: 		PrivateKey:  signer,

47: func startHTTPServer(addr, token, keyAuth string) *http.Server {

58: 	go func() {
59: 		// returns ErrServerClosed on graceful close
60: 		if err := srv.ListenAndServe(); err != http.ErrServerClosed {
61: 			// NOTE: there is a chance that next line won't have time to run,
62: 			// as main() doesn't wait for this goroutine to stop. don't use
63: 			// code with race conditions like these for production. see post

209: 		chValidated := false
210: 		for _, ch := range az.Challenges {
211: 			// TODO: Allow other types of challenges (not just http).
212: 			if ch.Type == "http-01" && !isAttest {
213: 				if err := serveAndValidateHTTPChallenge(ctx, ac, ch, ident); err != nil {
214: 					return err
215: 				}
216: 				chValidated = true
217: 				break
218: 			}
219: 			if ch.Type == "device-attest-01" && isAttest {
220: 				if err := doDeviceAttestation(ctx, ac, ch, ident, af); err != nil {
221: 					return err
222: 				}
223: 				chValidated = true
224: 				break
225: 			}
226: 		}
227: 		if !chValidated {
228: 			return errors.Errorf("unable to validate any challenges for identifier: %s", ident)
229: 		}
230: 	}
231: 	return nil
232: }

241: 	for i := 9; i >= 0; i-- {

248: 		if ro.Status == "ready" {

250: 			ui.Printf(" done!\n")
251: 			break

254: 	if !isReady {
255: 		ui.Printf(" Error!\n\n")

257: 	}

259: 	ui.Printf("Finalizing Order .")

285: func validateSANsForACME(sans []string) ([]string, []net.IP, error) {
286: 	dnsNames, ips, emails, uris := splitSANs(sans)
287: 	if len(emails) > 0 || len(uris) > 0 {
288: 		return nil, nil, errors.New("Email Address and URI SANs are not supported for ACME flow")
289: 	}

291: 		if strings.Contains(dns, "*") {
292: 			return nil, nil, errors.Errorf("wildcard dnsnames (%s) require dns validation, "+

299: func createNewOrderRequest(ctx *cli.Context, acmeDir, subject string, sans []string) (interface{}, []string, []net.IP, error) {
300: 	dnsNames, ips, err := validateSANsForACME(sans)
301: 	if err != nil {
302: 		return nil, nil, nil, err
303: 	}
304: 
305: 	var idents []acme.Identifier
306: 	for _, dns := range dnsNames {
307: 		idents = append(idents, acme.Identifier{
308: 			Type:  "dns",
309: 			Value: dns,
310: 		})
311: 	}
312: 	for _, ip := range ips {
313: 		idents = append(idents, acme.Identifier{
314: 			Type:  "ip",
315: 			Value: ip.String(),
316: 		})
317: 	}
318: 
319: 	if strings.Contains(acmeDir, "letsencrypt") {
320: 		// LetsEncrypt does not support NotBefore and NotAfter attributes in
321: 		// orders.
322: 		if ctx.IsSet("not-before") || ctx.IsSet("not-after") {
323: 			return nil, nil, nil, errors.New(
324: 				"LetsEncrypt public CA does not support NotBefore/NotAfter attributes for certificates. " +
325: 					"Instead, each certificate has a default lifetime of 3 months.",
326: 			)
327: 		}
328: 
329: 		// LetsEncrypt requires that the Common Name of the Certificate also be
330: 		// represented as a DNSName in the SAN extension, and therefore must be
331: 		// authorized as part of the ACME order.
332: 		hasSubject := false
333: 		for _, n := range idents {
334: 			if n.Value == subject {
335: 				hasSubject = true
336: 			}
337: 		}
338: 
339: 		if !hasSubject {
340: 			dnsNames = append(dnsNames, subject)
341: 			idents = append(idents, acme.Identifier{
342: 				Type:  "dns",
343: 				Value: subject,
344: 			})
345: 		}
346: 
347: 		return struct {
348: 			Identifiers []acme.Identifier
349: 		}{Identifiers: idents}, dnsNames, ips, nil
350: 	}
351: 
352: 	// parse times or durations
353: 	nbf, naf, err := flags.ParseTimeDuration(ctx)
354: 	if err != nil {
355: 		return nil, nil, nil, err
356: 	}
357: 
358: 	// check if the list of identifiers for which to request a certificate
359: 	// already contains the subject
360: 	hasSubject := false
361: 	for _, n := range idents {
362: 		if n.Value == subject {
363: 			hasSubject = true
364: 		}
365: 	}
366: 
367: 	// if the subject is not yet included in the slice of identifiers, it is
368: 	// added to either the DNS names or IP addresses slice and the corresponding
369: 	// type of identifier is added to the slice of identifiers.
370: 	if !hasSubject {
371: 		if ip := net.ParseIP(subject); ip != nil {
372: 			ips = append(ips, ip)
373: 			idents = append(idents, acme.Identifier{
374: 				Type:  "ip",
375: 				Value: ip.String(),
376: 			})
377: 		} else {
378: 			dnsNames = append(dnsNames, subject)
379: 			idents = append(idents, acme.Identifier{
380: 				Type:  "dns",
381: 				Value: subject,
382: 			})
383: 		}
384: 	}
385: 
386: 	return acmeAPI.NewOrderRequest{
387: 		Identifiers: idents,
388: 		NotAfter:    naf.Time(),
389: 		NotBefore:   nbf.Time(),
390: 	}, dnsNames, ips, nil
391: }

402: // doDeviceAttestation performs `device-attest-01` challenge validation.
403: func doDeviceAttestation(clictx *cli.Context, ac *ca.ACMEClient, ch *acme.Challenge, identifier string, af *acmeFlow) error {
404: 	// TODO(hs): make TPM flow work with CreateAttestor()/Attest() too
405: 	attestationURI := clictx.String("attestation-uri")
406: 	if strings.HasPrefix(attestationURI, "tpmkms:") {
407: 		return doTPMAttestation(clictx, ac, ch, identifier, af)
408: 	}
409: 
410: 	attestor, err := cryptoutil.CreateAttestor("", attestationURI)
411: 	if err != nil {
412: 		return err
413: 	}
414: 	pemData, err := attestor.Attest()
415: 	if err != nil {
416: 		return err
417: 	}
418: 
419: 	data, err := acme.KeyAuthorization(ch.Token, ac.Key)
420: 	if err != nil {
421: 		return errors.Wrap(err, "error generating ACME key authorization")
422: 	}
423: 
424: 	var alg int64
425: 	var digest []byte
426: 	var opts crypto.SignerOpts
427: 	switch k := attestor.Public().(type) {
428: 	case *ecdsa.PublicKey:
429: 		if k.Curve != elliptic.P256() {
430: 			return fmt.Errorf("unsupported elliptic curve %s", k.Curve)
431: 		}
432: 		alg = -7 // ES256
433: 		opts = crypto.SHA256
434: 		sum := sha256.Sum256([]byte(data))
435: 		digest = sum[:]
436: 	case *rsa.PublicKey:
437: 		// TODO(mariano): support for PS256 (-37)
438: 		alg = -257 // RS256
439: 		opts = crypto.SHA256
440: 		sum := sha256.Sum256([]byte(data))
441: 		digest = sum[:]
442: 	case ed25519.PublicKey:
443: 		alg = -8 // EdDSA
444: 		opts = crypto.Hash(0)
445: 		digest = []byte(data)
446: 	default:
447: 		return fmt.Errorf("unsupported public key type %T", k)
448: 	}
449: 
450: 	// Sign proves possession of private key. Per recommendation at
451: 	// https://w3c.github.io/webauthn/#sctn-signature-attestation-types, we use
452: 	// CBOR to encode the signature.
453: 	sig, err := attestor.Sign(rand.Reader, digest, opts)
454: 	if err != nil {
455: 		return errors.Wrap(err, "error signing key authorization")
456: 	}
457: 	sig, err = cbor.Marshal(sig)
458: 	if err != nil {
459: 		return errors.Wrap(err, "error marshaling signature")
460: 	}
461: 
462: 	certs, err := pemutil.ParseCertificateBundle(pemData)
463: 	if err != nil {
464: 		return err
465: 	}
466: 
467: 	x5c := make([][]byte, len(certs))
468: 	for i, c := range certs {
469: 		x5c[i] = c.Raw
470: 	}
471: 
472: 	// step format is based on the "packed" format described in
473: 	// https://w3c.github.io/webauthn/#sctn-attestation but with the authData
474: 	// omitted as described in the device-attest-01 RFC.
475: 	obj := &attestationObject{
476: 		Format: "step",
477: 		AttStatement: map[string]interface{}{
478: 			"alg": alg,
479: 			"sig": sig,
480: 			"x5c": x5c,
481: 		},
482: 	}
483: 
484: 	b, err := cbor.Marshal(obj)
485: 	if err != nil {
486: 		return err
487: 	}
488: 
489: 	payload, err := json.Marshal(attestationPayload{
490: 		AttObj: base64.RawURLEncoding.EncodeToString(b),
491: 	})
492: 	if err != nil {
493: 		return fmt.Errorf("error marshaling payload: %w", err)
494: 	}
495: 
496: 	ui.Printf("Using Device Attestation challenge to validate %q", identifier)
497: 	ui.Printf(" .") // Indicates passage of time.
498: 
499: 	if err := ac.ValidateWithPayload(ch.URL, payload); err != nil {
500: 		ui.Printf(" Error!\n\n")
501: 		return errors.Wrapf(err, "error validating ACME Challenge at %s", ch.URL)
502: 	}
503: 
504: 	durationBetweenAttempts := 2 * time.Second
505: 	if err := getChallengeStatus(ac, ch, durationBetweenAttempts); err != nil {
506: 		ui.Printf(" Error!\n\n")
507: 		return err
508: 	}
509: 
510: 	ui.Printf(" done!\n")
511: 	return nil
512: }
513: 
514: // getChallengeStatus retrieves the ACME Challenge status from the CA. It
515: // will retry this 10 times if the status is not `invalid` or `valid`. This
516: // is the case, for example, when the CA hasn't been able to connect to the
517: // HTTP endpoint for some reason.
518: func getChallengeStatus(ac *ca.ACMEClient, ch *acme.Challenge, durationBetweenAttempts time.Duration) error {
519: 	var (
520: 		isValid = false
521: 		vch     *acme.Challenge
522: 		err     error
523: 	)
524: 	for attempts := 0; attempts < 10; attempts++ {
525: 		vch, err = ac.GetChallenge(ch.URL) // TODO(hs): GetChallenge should return an ACME GetChallenge client response type; not core acme.Challenge type (for safety)
526: 		if err != nil {
527: 			return errors.Wrapf(err, "error retrieving ACME Challenge at %s", ch.URL)
528: 		}
529: 		// break early if challenge validation failed. Due to nature of the `device-attest-01`
530: 		// challenge validation, this will (currently) happen immediately, as the validation is
531: 		// performed synchronously by the CA when the request for `ac.ValidateWithPayload` is
532: 		// sent. For `http-01`, this is the case when the key authorization doesn't match.
533: 		// In the (near) future we might change the way the validation is performed, so keeping
534: 		// the retry logic intact for now.
535: 		if vch.Status == "invalid" {
536: 			break
537: 		}
538: 		if vch.Status == "valid" {
539: 			isValid = true
540: 			break
541: 		}
542: 		ui.Printf(".")
543: 		time.Sleep(durationBetweenAttempts)
544: 	}
545: 	if !isValid {
546: 		return errors.New(extractDetailedErrorMessageFromChallenge(vch))
547: 	}
548: 	return nil
549: }
550: 
551: // extractDetailedErrorMessageFromChallenge extracts error details from an
552: // ACME Challenge if the server captured an error when validating it. When
553: // the ACME Error has one or more Subproblems, the details will be extracted
554: // from those. Otherwise, the main Error detail will be used. In case the
555: // server did not return an Error for the Challenge, a textual representation
556: // of the Challenge is printed as fallback.
557: func extractDetailedErrorMessageFromChallenge(vch *acme.Challenge) string {
558: 	switch {
559: 	case vch.Error == nil:
560: 		// fallback to original error message
561: 		return fmt.Sprintf("Unable to validate challenge: %+v", vch)
562: 	case len(vch.Error.Subproblems) == 1:
563: 		if detail := vch.Error.Subproblems[0].Detail; detail != "" {
564: 			return fmt.Sprintf("Unable to validate challenge: %s", detail)
565: 		}
566: 		fallthrough // subproblem detail empty; fallthrough to the error
567: 	case len(vch.Error.Subproblems) > 1:
568: 		details := make([]string, len(vch.Error.Subproblems))
569: 		for i, s := range vch.Error.Subproblems {
570: 			if s.Detail == "" {
571: 				details[i] = fmt.Sprintf("%+v", s)
572: 			} else {
573: 				details[i] = s.Detail
574: 			}
575: 		}
576: 		return fmt.Sprintf("Unable to validate challenge: %s", strings.Join(details, "; "))
577: 	case vch.Error.Detail == "":
578: 		// fallback to original error message
579: 		return fmt.Sprintf("Unable to validate challenge: %+v", vch)
580: 	default:
581: 		return fmt.Sprintf("Unable to validate challenge: %s", vch.Error.Detail)
582: 	}
583: }

625: func newACMEFlow(ctx *cli.Context, ops ...acmeFlowOp) (*acmeFlow, error) {
626: 	// Offline mode is not supported for ACME protocol
627: 	if ctx.Bool("offline") {
628: 		return nil, errors.New("offline mode and ACME are mutually exclusive")
629: 	}
630: 	// One of --standalone or --webroot must be selected for use with ACME protocol.
631: 	isStandalone, webroot := ctx.Bool("standalone"), ctx.String("webroot")
632: 	switch {
633: 	case isStandalone && webroot != "":
634: 		return nil, errs.MutuallyExclusiveFlags(ctx, "standalone", "webroot")
635: 	case !isStandalone && webroot == "":
636: 		if err := ctx.Set("standalone", "true"); err != nil {
637: 			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "error setting 'standalone' value in cli ctx")
638: 		}
639: 	}
640: 
641: 	af := new(acmeFlow)
642: 	for _, op := range ops {
643: 		if err := op(af); err != nil {
644: 			return nil, err
645: 		}
646: 	}
647: 	if len(af.sans) == 0 {
648: 		af.sans = []string{af.subject}
649: 	}
650: 
651: 	af.ctx = ctx
652: 
653: 	af.acmeDir = ctx.String("acme")
654: 	if af.acmeDir == "" {
655: 		caURL, err := flags.ParseCaURL(ctx)
656: 		if err != nil {
657: 			return nil, err
658: 		}
659: 		if af.provisionerName == "" {
660: 			return nil, errors.New("acme flow expected provisioner ID")
661: 		}
662: 		af.acmeDir = fmt.Sprintf("%s/acme/%s/directory", caURL, af.provisionerName)
663: 	}
664: 
665: 	return af, nil
666: }

668: func (af *acmeFlow) getClientTruststoreOption(mergeRootCAs bool) (ca.ClientOption, error) {
669: 	root := ""
670: 	if af.ctx.IsSet("root") {
671: 		root = af.ctx.String("root")
672: 		// If there's an error reading the local root ca, ignore the error and use the system store
673: 	} else if _, err := os.Stat(pki.GetRootCAPath()); err == nil {
674: 		root = pki.GetRootCAPath()
675: 	}
676: 
677: 	// 1. Merge local RootCA with system store
678: 	if mergeRootCAs && root != "" {
679: 		rootCAs, err := x509.SystemCertPool()
680: 		if err != nil || rootCAs == nil {
681: 			rootCAs = x509.NewCertPool()
682: 		}
683: 
684: 		cert, err := os.ReadFile(root)
685: 		if err != nil {
686: 			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to read local root ca")
687: 		}
688: 
689: 		if ok := rootCAs.AppendCertsFromPEM(cert); !ok {
690: 			return nil, errors.New("failed to append local root ca to system cert pool")
691: 		}
692: 
693: 		return ca.WithTransport(&http.Transport{
694: 			TLSClientConfig: &tls.Config{
695: 				RootCAs:    rootCAs,
696: 				MinVersion: tls.VersionTLS12,
697: 			},
698: 		}), nil
699: 	}
700: 
701: 	// Use local Root CA only
702: 	if root != "" {
703: 		return ca.WithRootFile(root), nil
704: 	}
705: 
706: 	// Use system store only
707: 	return ca.WithTransport(http.DefaultTransport), nil
708: }

710: func (af *acmeFlow) GetCertificate() ([]*x509.Certificate, error) {
711: 	var (
712: 		err             error
713: 		newOrderRequest interface{}
714: 		dnsNames        []string
715: 		ips             []net.IP
716: 	)
717: 
718: 	attestationURI := af.ctx.String("attestation-uri")
719: 	if attestationURI == "" {
720: 		newOrderRequest, dnsNames, ips, err = createNewOrderRequest(af.ctx, af.acmeDir, af.subject, af.sans)
721: 		if err != nil {
722: 			return nil, err
723: 		}
724: 	} else {
725: 		// parse times or durations
726: 		nbf, naf, err := flags.ParseTimeDuration(af.ctx)
727: 		if err != nil {
728: 			return nil, err
729: 		}
730: 
731: 		// We currently do not accept other SANs with attestation certificates.
732: 		newOrderRequest = acmeAPI.NewOrderRequest{
733: 			Identifiers: []acme.Identifier{{
734: 				Type:  "permanent-identifier",
735: 				Value: af.subject,
736: 			}},
737: 			NotBefore: nbf.Time(),
738: 			NotAfter:  naf.Time(),
739: 		}
740: 	}
741: 
742: 	orderPayload, err := json.Marshal(newOrderRequest)
743: 	if err != nil {
744: 		return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "error marshaling order request")
745: 	}
746: 
747: 	ops, err := af.getClientTruststoreOption(af.ctx.IsSet("acme"))
748: 	if err != nil {
749: 		return nil, err
750: 	}
751: 
752: 	ac, err := ca.NewACMEClient(af.acmeDir, af.ctx.StringSlice("contact"), ops)
753: 	if err != nil {
754: 		return nil, errors.Wrapf(err, "error initializing ACME client with server %s", af.acmeDir)
755: 	}
756: 
757: 	o, err := ac.NewOrder(orderPayload)
758: 	if err != nil {
759: 		return nil, errors.Wrapf(err, "error creating new ACME order")
760: 	}
761: 
762: 	if err := authorizeOrder(af.ctx, ac, o, af); err != nil {
763: 		return nil, err
764: 	}
765: 
766: 	if af.csr == nil {
767: 		var signer crypto.Signer
768: 		var template *x509.CertificateRequest
769: 		switch {
770: 		case attestationURI == "":
771: 			insecure := af.ctx.Bool("insecure")
772: 			kty, crv, size, err := utils.GetKeyDetailsFromCLI(af.ctx, insecure, "kty", "curve", "size")
773: 			if err != nil {
774: 				return nil, err
775: 			}
776: 			signer, err = keyutil.GenerateSigner(kty, crv, size)
777: 			if err != nil {
778: 				return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "error generating private key")
779: 			}
780: 			af.priv = signer
781: 			template = &x509.CertificateRequest{
782: 				Subject: pkix.Name{
783: 					CommonName: af.subject,
784: 				},
785: 				DNSNames:    dnsNames,
786: 				IPAddresses: ips,
787: 			}
788: 		case af.tpmSigner != nil:
789: 			signer = af.tpmSigner
790: 			template = &x509.CertificateRequest{
791: 				Subject: pkix.Name{
792: 					CommonName: af.subject,
793: 				},
794: 				// TODO(hs): add PermanentIdentifier extension?
795: 				// TODO(hs): add SKAE extension?
796: 			}
797: 		default:
798: 			signer, err = cryptoutil.CreateSigner(attestationURI, attestationURI)
799: 			if err != nil {
800: 				return nil, err
801: 			}
802: 			template = &x509.CertificateRequest{
803: 				Subject: pkix.Name{
804: 					CommonName: af.subject,

/Users/max/.step/authorities/machine.step-internal.net
'''

Get the base path:
'''
$ step path --base
/Users/max/.step
'''

Get the base path with environment variable STEPPATH overriding the default:
'''
$ export STEPPATH=/tmp/step
$ step path --base
/tmp/step
'''

/Users/max/.step/profiles/beta-corp
'''
`,

				Usage: "Return the base path of the currently configured default profile",

				return nil
			}

350: // checkKeyDetails checks that the public/private key pair is valid. It performs
351: // the following checks:
352: //
353: //   - Compare the public and private key SHA-1 thumbprints to verify they match
354: //   - The type of the key that was created
355: //   - For RSA keys, the key size is the expected size, and using the expected algorithm
356: //   - For EC keys, the key curve is the expected curve, and using the expected algorithm
357: //   - For OKP keys, the key curve is the expected curve, and using the expected algorithm
358: //   - For oct keys, the key parts are of the expected type, and using the expected algorithm
359: func checkKeyDetails(ts *testscript.TestScript, pub, priv *jose.JSONWebKey, args []string) {
360: 	keyType := strings.ToUpper(args[2])
361: 	if keyType == "OCT" {
362: 		if _, ok := pub.Key.([]byte); !ok {
363: 			ts.Fatalf("expected public key %s to be a byte slice; got %T", args[0], pub.Key)
364: 		}
365: 		if _, ok := priv.Key.([]byte); !ok {
366: 			ts.Fatalf("expected private key %s to be a byte slice; got %T", args[0], pub.Key)
367: 		}
368: 	} else {
369: 		pubHash, err := pub.Thumbprint(crypto.SHA1)
370: 		ts.Check(err)
371: 		privHash, err := priv.Thumbprint(crypto.SHA1)
372: 		ts.Check(err)
373: 
374: 		if !bytes.Equal(pubHash, privHash) {
375: 			ts.Fatalf("%s and %s have different thumbprints", args[0], args[1])
376: 		}
377: 	}
378: 
379: 	switch {
380: 	case keyType == "RSA":
381: 		if !strings.HasPrefix(pub.Algorithm, "RS") && !strings.HasPrefix(pub.Algorithm, "PS") {
382: 			ts.Fatalf("expected RSA algorithm for RSA key, got %q", pub.Algorithm)
383: 		}
384: 
385: 		expectedLength, err := strconv.Atoi(args[3])
386: 		ts.Check(err)
387: 
388: 		length, err := keyLength(pub)
389: 		ts.Check(err)
390: 
391: 		if length != expectedLength {
392: 			ts.Fatalf("key length mismatch: expected %d, got %d", expectedLength, length)
393: 		}
394: 
395: 		if len(args) > 4 {
396: 			expectedAlgorithm := args[4]
397: 			if !strings.EqualFold(pub.Algorithm, expectedAlgorithm) {
398: 				ts.Fatalf("key algorithm mismatch: expected %s, got %s", expectedAlgorithm, pub.Algorithm)
399: 			}
400: 		}
401: 
402: 		return
403: 	case keyType == "OKP":
404: 		if !strings.HasPrefix(pub.Algorithm, "EdDSA") {
405: 			ts.Fatalf("expected EC algorithm for EC key, got %q", pub.Algorithm)
406: 		}
407: 
408: 		if crv := strings.ToUpper(args[3]); crv != "ED25519" {
409: 			ts.Fatalf("unexpected OKP curve %q", args[3])
410: 		}
411: 	case keyType == "OCT":
412: 		if !strings.HasPrefix(pub.Algorithm, "HS") && !strings.HasPrefix(pub.Algorithm, "A") && pub.Algorithm != "dir" {
413: 			ts.Fatalf("expected oct algorithm for oct key, got %q", pub.Algorithm)
414: 		}
415: 
416: 		expectedAlgorithm := args[3]
417: 		if !strings.EqualFold(pub.Algorithm, expectedAlgorithm) {
418: 			ts.Fatalf("key algorithm mismatch: expected %s, got %s", expectedAlgorithm, pub.Algorithm)
419: 		}
420: 	case strings.HasPrefix(keyType, "EC"):
421: 		if !strings.HasPrefix(pub.Algorithm, "ES") && !strings.HasPrefix(pub.Algorithm, "ECDH") {
422: 			ts.Fatalf("expected EC algorithm for EC key, got %q", pub.Algorithm)
423: 		}
424: 
425: 		if len(args) > 4 {
426: 			expectedAlgorithm := args[4]
427: 			if !strings.EqualFold(pub.Algorithm, expectedAlgorithm) {
428: 				ts.Fatalf("key algorithm mismatch: expected %s, got %s", expectedAlgorithm, pub.Algorithm)
429: 			}
430: 		}
431: 
432: 		kc, err := keyCurve(pub)
433: 		ts.Check(err)
434: 
435: 		switch crv := strings.ToUpper(args[3]); crv {
436: 		case "P-256":
437: 			if kc != elliptic.P256() {
438: 				ts.Fatalf("expected P-256 curve, got %q", kc)
439: 			}
440: 		case "P-384":
441: 			if kc != elliptic.P384() {
442: 				ts.Fatalf("expected P-384 curve, got %q", kc)
443: 			}
444: 		case "P-521":
445: 			if kc != elliptic.P521() {
446: 				ts.Fatalf("expected P-521 curve, got %q", kc)
447: 			}
448: 		default:
449: 			ts.Fatalf("unknown curve %q", crv)
450: 		}
451: 	default:
452: 		ts.Fatalf("unknown key format %q", args[2])
453: 	}
454: }

456: func keyLength(jwk *jose.JSONWebKey) (int, error) {

464: 	case *ecdsa.PrivateKey:

input.content:
---
type: concept
title: Online and Offline CA Flows
description: How the step CLI signs, renews, revokes, and rekeys certificates, unifying the online step-ca HTTP client and the embedded offline authority through the cautils CaClient abstraction and the ACME device/HTTP challenge flow.
tags: [ca-flows, offline-mode, ca-client, acme-flow, certificate-lifecycle]
---

# Online and Offline CA Flows

The `step ca` certificate lifecycle commands must work both against a running
`step-ca` server (online mode) and against an embedded copy of the authority's
signing logic using the configuration produced by `step ca init` (offline mode).
A single interface, `cautils.CaClient`, plus a shared certificate flow, unify the
two paths so command actions do not branch on the backend for every operation.

## The CaClient abstraction

`cautils.CaClient` (in `utils/cautils/client.go`) is the interface implemented
by both the online client and the offline wrapper. It exposes the full lifecycle:
`Sign`, `Renew`, `RenewWithToken`, `Revoke`, `Rekey`, the SSH family
(`SSHSign`, `SSHRenew`, `SSHRekey`, `SSHRevoke`, `SSHRoots`, `SSHFederation`,
`SSHConfig`, `SSHCheckHost`, `SSHGetHosts`, `SSHBastion`), plus `Version`,
`GetRootCAs`, and `GetCaURL`.

`cautils.NewClient` selects the implementation from the CLI context: if
`--offline` is set it requires a `--ca-config` and returns a `NewOfflineCA`;
otherwise it parses `--ca-url` (HTTPS) and `--root` and returns an online
`ca.NewClient` rooted with `ca.WithRootFile`. When clients are constructed from a
bootstrap/style provisioning token in `CertificateFlow.GetClient`, the token's
root SHA (`ca.WithRootSHA256`) replaces the file-based root so `ca-url` may be
derived from the token audience.

## The certificate flow

`CertificateFlow` (`utils/cautils/certificate_flow.go`) drives the steps behind
`step ca certificate` and `step ca sign`. `NewCertificateFlow` reads `--offline`
and, when set, instantiates the `OfflineCA` from `--ca-config`; otherwise it
stays online. Flow options (`WithSSHPublicKey`, `WithCertificateRequest`,
`WithConfirmationFingerprint`, `WithCustomAttributes`) mutate a package-level
`sharedContext` used when generating tokens.

For an untokenized request, `GenerateToken` either calls `offlineCA.GenerateToken`
or builds a token online. `CreateSignRequest` generates a fresh key pair via
`utils.GetKeyDetailsFromCLI`/`keyutil.GenerateKey`, derives SANs per token type
(AWS instance document, GCP compute engine, Azure resource name, OIDC email/subject,
K8sSA subject, or the JWK subject using the common-name-in-token default), and
returns an X.509 CSR alongside the private key. `Sign` parses `--not-before`/
`--not-after` and `--set`/`--set-file` template data, submits an
`api.SignRequest`, and writes the returned certificate chain to the output file.

## OfflineCA: an embedded authority

`OfflineCA` (`utils/cautils/offline.go`) wraps the `step-ca` `authority.Authority`
type directly, using the `ca.json` loaded from `--ca-config`. Because double
initialization can be unsafe for some storage backends (e.g. badger locking), the
instance is a singleton (`offlineInstance`). Its `GetCaURL` and `CaURL` return
`https://` + the first configured DNS name, and `Audience` maps token types to the
equivalent `https://` paths used by the online API.

Each lifecycle method wraps the authority call and reuses the token audience and
signing logic:
- `Sign` calls `authority.Authorize` then `SignWithContext`.
- `Renew`/`Rekey` recover the peer certificate from the mTLS transport's
  client certificate and call `authority.Renew`/`Rekey`.
- `RenewWithToken` calls `authority.AuthorizeRenewToken` then `Renew`.
- `Revoke` authorizes via an OTT or the mTLS certificate and calls `authority.Revoke`
  with `PassiveOnly` as configured.
- `SSHSign`, `SSHRenew`, `SSHRekey`, `SSHRevoke`, `SSHRoots`, `SSHFederation`,
  `SSHConfig`, `SSHCheckHost`, `SSHGetHosts`, and `SSHBastion` wrap the
  corresponding authority SSH methods.

The offline instance's `GenerateToken` mirrors the online token flow
(`offline.go#GenerateToken`) using the `ca.json` root and audience and dispatching
per provisioner type, with the same unsupported types returning sentinel errors.

## Online lifecycle commands

`step ca certificate` (`command/ca/certificate.go`) validates flag combinations
(such as `--offline` being incompatible with `--token`, and `--attestation-uri`
being incompatible with `--kms`), then creates a `CertificateFlow`. If no token
is supplied it either enters the ACME flow (when `--acme` is set) or generates a
token; if the generated token signals an ACME provisioner (an `ACMETokenError`)
it delegates to `ACMECreateCertFlow`. The token type is inspected with
`token.ParseInsecure`: JWK tokens must match the CSR subject exactly, while
OIDC/AWS/GCP/Azure/K8sSA subjects are validated server-side already.

`step ca sign` (`command/ca/sign.go`) does the same through
`cautils.ACMESignCSRFlow` when appropriate)Skip.

## Renew and Revoke

`step ca renew` (`command/ca/renew.go`) builds a `renewer` that wraps a
`cautils.CaClient` and an `http.Transport` configured with the configured root as
trust anchorring certificates. By default renew uses mTLS; `--mtls=false` forces a
token-based `X5cInsecure` flow, which is also used automatically once the current
certificate has expired (`RenewWithToken`). The single-shot path skips renewal if
`--expires-in` is not yet within the remaining validity plus a jitter. The daemon
(`--daemon`) loops on a timer, renewing before 2/3 of validity, and can signal a
PID, read a PID file, or run an `--exec` command after each renewal. `nextRenewDuration`
computes the sleep, adding random jitter so fleet-wide renewals are not synchronized.

`step ca revoke` (`command/ca/revoke.go`) supports authorization by a transparently
generated JWK provisioner token (keyed on the serial number) or by mTLS using
`--cert`/`--key`. It maps the `--reasonCode` text/number to an OCSP code via
`ReasonCodeToNum`/`RevocationReasonCodes` and always sends passive revocation
(`Passive: true`) — the command notes in source that it only supports passive
revocation (preventing renewal) and that active CRL/OCSP revocation is a TODO.

## The ACME flow

The ACME path (`utils/cautils/acme_flow.go` / `acmeutils.go`) is only for cert
creation and CSR signing; it is mutually exclusive with offline mode
(`newACMEFlow` returns an error if `--offline` is set). The flow selects either a
standalone HTTP server on a listener (`--standalone`, the default) or a webroot
directory (`--webroot`) to answer `http-01` challenges, or the `device-attest-01`
challenge when an `--attestation-uri` is supplied)Skip).

`authorizeOrder` walks each authorization, chooses the matching challenge type,
and calls `serveAndValidateHTTPChallenge` (or `doDeviceAttestation`). The flow
then waits for the order to become `ready`, finalizes it with a CSR, polls until
`valid`, and downloads the certificate chain. The CA directory defaults to
`<ca-url>/acme/<provisioner>/directory` when no explicit `--acme` URL is given.

For device attestation, `doDeviceAttestation` produces a CBOR-serialized "step"
format attestation object (signing the key authorization) and submits it via
`ac.ValidateWithPayload`. When the attestation URI is `tpmkms:`, a separate
TPM signer and directory storage flow is used (`af.tpmSigner`).

## Relationship to tokens

Both flows depend on the token system: online flows derive the audience and root
from flags or the token's audience/SHA, and offline flows use the `ca.json`
derived audience and root. Provisioner selection is shared through
`provisionerPrompt` in `utils/cautils/token_flow.go`, which filters by type,
`--kid`, `--provisioner`/`--issuer`, and `--admin-provisioner`. Provisioners that
do not support token auth return `ACMETokenError` or `SCEPTokenError`, prompting
the command to fall back to the ACME/SCEP-specific flows.

CertificateFlow.CreateSignRequest generates a fresh key pair and derives the CSR SANs per token type (AWS instance document, GCP compute engine, Azure resource, OIDC email/subject, K8sSA subject, or the JWK common-name default).
CertificateFlow.Sign parses --not-before/--not-after and template data, submits an api.SignRequest, and writes the returned certificate chain to the requested output file.
